label.en: 🗻 ACT Math — Official Reporting Categories (enhanced ACT: 45 questions, 50 min)

body.en:
Reporting Category% of TestKey Topics
Preparing for Higher Mathematics80%Broken into 5 sub-areas below
   · Number & Quantity10–12%Integers, ratios, percents, complex numbers, vectors, matrices
   · Algebra17–20%Linear/quadratic equations, systems, inequalities, absolute value
   · Functions17–20%Definition, notation, graphs, transformations, composition, inverse
   · Geometry17–20%Area, volume, angle relationships, trig, coordinate geometry
   · Statistics & Probability12–15%Mean/median/mode, data interpretation, probability, expected value
Integrating Essential Skills20%Multi-step problems spanning rates, percentages, proportions, measurement, area/volume

The enhanced ACT Math test (from September 2025) is 45 multiple-choice questions in 50 minutes — about 67 seconds each — and a calculator is allowed throughout. 41 questions are scored; 4 are unscored field-test items you can't identify, so answer every one. Questions run roughly easy to hard, drawing on everything from pre-algebra to trigonometry.

Four answer choices per question (the enhanced ACT dropped the fifth). There is no formula sheet, so the key formulas must be memorized. The content spans number & quantity, algebra, functions, geometry, and statistics & probability.
Don't linger — flag a hard item and move on so easy points aren't lost. Backsolve from the answer choices, and plug in convenient numbers for variables when a question is abstract.

• Questions 1–15 (Easy): Spend ~40 seconds per question (10 minutes total). Bank time early while building confidence.
  • Questions 16–30 (Medium): Spend ~65 seconds per question (16 minutes total). Watch for multi-step algebra and word problems.
  • Questions 31–45 (Hard): Spend ~85 seconds per question (21 minutes total). These feature advanced geometry, trigonometry, and novel combinations.
  • Final 3 Minutes: Check flagged items and ensure EVERY single question has a bubbled answer!

• No Negative Marking: There is absolutely no penalty for wrong answers on the ACT. An unanswered question is guaranteed 0 points; an educated guess gives a 25% to 50% chance of a point.
  • 4-Choice Format: Enhanced ACT has 4 options (A, B, C, D) instead of 5, boosting blind guessing accuracy from 20% to 25%. Eliminating just one obvious wrong answer raises your odds to 33.3%, and eliminating two gives a 50% coin-flip.
  • Letter of the Day: If running out of time on the last 3–4 questions, pick one consistent letter (e.g., C) for all remaining items rather than alternating randomly.
